<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A function $u \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ is an entire local minimizer of the functional $\hat{J}$ from (1.8), iff
\begin{equation}
    \hat{J}[u, \Omega] \le \hat{J}[v, \Omega]
\end{equation}
holds for all bounded domains $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ and any $v \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ such that $u = v$ outside of a compact subset of $\Omega$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
Let (1.2)--(1.4) hold for the density $f$ and consider an entire local $\hat{J}$-minimizer $u \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ as in Definition 1.1. Then, if $u$ is bounded, the constancy of $u$ follows.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
The Liouville property for entire local minimizers of variational integrals or for entire solutions of various types of elliptic equations has been investigated during the past decades by many authors. For an overview we refer to the nice work [5] or to the references given in Section 1 of [6].
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
Since the density $f$ is of linear growth, one might even ask, if the Bernstein property holds for entire local minimizers $u$ under additional assumptions imposed on $f$, which means that without further hypotheses concerning $u$ the function $u$ must be affine. Actually we have no idea, if this can be achieved, or if non-affine counterexamples exist.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
Under the assumptions (1.2), (1.3) and (1.4) concerning the density $f$ consider an entire local $\hat{J}$-minimizer $u \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ in the sense of Definition 1.1. Then, if $\nabla^a u = 0$ holds, $u$ must be a constant function.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
Let the density $f$ satisfy (1.2)--(1.4) and consider entire local $\hat{J}$-minimizers $u_1, u_2 \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ in the sense of Definition 1.1. Suppose that $u_1 - u_2 \in L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ and that $u_i \in C^2(\mathbb{R}^2, \mathbb{R}^N)$ for at least one index $i$. Then we have the constancy of $u_1 - u_2$, provided $f(p) = g(|p|)$ with $g \in C^2([0,\infty))$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
For the interested reader we note that the result of Theorem 2.1 is not necessarily based on the structure condition $f(p) = g(|p|)$, $p \in \mathbb{R}^{2N}$. Actually it holds, if the density $f$ is an even function with the properties (1.2)--(1.4). In fact, exactly the same calculations (see (2.14) and compare the discussion after this equation) will lead to the identity\begin{equation}f_\infty\left(\frac{\nabla^s u_1}{|\nabla^s u_1|}\right) = \nabla f(\nabla u_2) \cdot \frac{\nabla^s u_1}{|\nabla^s u_1|}\end{equation}for $|\nabla^s u_1|$-almost all points. Now, from (1.2)--(1.4) we get the strict inequality$$ f_\infty(p) > \nabla f(q) \cdot p $$valid for all choices of $p$ and $q$ with $p \neq 0$, hence (2.15) shows that $\nabla^s u_1$ must vanish.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Let us consider the more geometric case that $N = 1$. Clearly any affine function $v : \mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is an entire local minimizer, and Theorem 2.1 implies that in any $L^\infty$-neighborhood of such a plane no other surface being the graph of an entire local $BV$-minimizer $\mathbb{R}^2 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ exists.
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
Let $N = 1$ and consider a density $f \in C^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ with (1.2)--(1.4) being of the type $f(p) = g(|p|)$, $p \in \mathbb{R}^2$, for a function $g \in C^2([0,\infty))$. If $u \in BV_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ denotes an entire local $\hat{J}$-minimizer in the sense of Definition 1.1 being bounded from one side, then $u$ is constant.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
We leave open to decide, whether the structure condition for $f$ is really necessary.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
Let $\mu$ be a $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued measure on the measure space $(X, \Sigma)$ such that $|\mu|(X) < \infty$, where $|\mu|$ is the total variation of $\mu$ (see [3], Definition 1.4, p.3). Let $g \in L^1(X, |\mu|)$ such that $g \ge 0$ $|\mu|$-almost everywhere and define the $\mathbb{R}^m$-valued measure $\widetilde{\mu} := \mu \lfloor g$, i.e. $\widetilde{\mu}(B) = \int_B g  \mathrm{d}\mu$, $B \in \Sigma$. Then it holds$$ |\widetilde{\mu}| = |\mu| \lfloor g. $$
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We quote [3], Corollary 1.29, p.14, to get $\mu = |\mu| \lfloor E$, $\widetilde{\mu} = |\widetilde{\mu}| \lfloor \widetilde{E}$ with $S^{m-1}$-valued functions $E, \widetilde{E}$. Moreover, it holds $|\widetilde{\mu}| \ll |\mu|$: if $B \in \Sigma$ such that $|\mu|(B) = 0$, then we get$$ \widetilde{\mu}(B) = \int_B g  \mathrm{d}\mu = \int_B g E  \mathrm{d}|\mu| = 0, $$hence $\widetilde{\mu} \ll |\mu|$, and in conclusion $|\widetilde{\mu}| \ll |\mu|$. By the Radon-Nikodym theorem ([3], Theorem 1.28, p.14) we find $\Theta \in L^1(X, |\mu|)$, $\Theta \ge 0$, such that $|\widetilde{\mu}| = |\mu| \lfloor \Theta$. For any set $B$ we get:$$ \widetilde{\mu}(B) = \int_B g  \mathrm{d}\mu = \int_B g E  \mathrm{d}|\mu| $$and at the same time$$ \widetilde{\mu}(B) = \int_B \widetilde{E}  \mathrm{d}|\widetilde{\mu}| = \int_B \widetilde{E} \Theta  \mathrm{d}|\mu|, $$so that$$ g E = \widetilde{E} \Theta \quad \text{almost everywhere.} $$Recalling $|E| = 1$, $|\widetilde{E}| = 1$, $\Theta, g \ge 0$ we deduce $g \equiv \Theta$, which proves our claim.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
